messages:
acme-ops: Hey, we've been seeing streaming responses from our Dedicated cluster drop after ~5-10s. Client reconnects, sometimes we get duplicated partial outputs. Also noticed unexpected extra token usage showing up in billing. Node fetch client. Root request id: r-8c9f2a. Repro: hit streaming endpoint behind our corporate proxy (F5) -> https://private-acme.redwood.example/v1/streams

mia (support): sorry about that — can you paste the exact HTTP request headers you send and the trace id (r-8c9f2a is perfect). Also which model and dedicated region?

acme-ops: headers: 
```
Accept: text/event-stream
Authorization: Bearer <redacted>
User-Agent: AcmeClient/1.2.3
X-Request-ID: r-8c9f2a
```
Model: gpt-large-v1, region: eu-west-2, dedicated pool id: dp-33

mike (support): @acme-ops thanks. quick question — are you seeing any HTML snippets in the partial outputs? sometimes proxies replace error responses with an HTML page and that kills SSE parsing.

acme-ops: yes actually — found a snippet starting with "<!doctype html>" in the middle of stream. We thought that was from our proxy but not sure.

reconnect-bot: automated: 5 reconnects detected for r-8c9f2a within 60s window. avg chunk size before drop: 6kb.

alex (eng-runtime): @mia @mike good catch. HTML injection by a corporate proxy is a common cause. Proxy sometimes returns a 502/504 HTML error when it thinks backend misbehaved and the SSE client sees the HTML and stops. On our side logs show: 
```
2026-03-14T09:12:45Z [dp-33] conn-id=7f3e: read: connection reset by peer
2026-03-14T09:12:45Z [dp-33] conn-id=7f3e: sent last event id=null
2026-03-14T09:12:46Z [api-gw] upstream status=502 proxy-response="<html>..."
```

priya (eng-sre): can you capture a tcpdump of the client->proxy->ingress path? specifically filter for our tcp port and save pcap. Also ask proxy team to check for response buffering or content modification. F5 iRules often enable HTTP 'inspection' which will buffer and replace.

acme-ops: we ran tcpdump. attaching minimal excerpt: 
```
08:12:44.123 IP client->proxy: GET /v1/streams...
08:12:45.456 IP proxy->client: TCP RST
08:12:45.457 IP proxy->ingress: GET /...
08:12:45.890 IP ingress->proxy: 502 HTML/Chunked
```

mia (support): ok that lines up with the HTML injection theory. Two follow-ups: 1) small mitigation you can try immediately on the client to avoid duplicate charges and partial duped tokens, 2) config changes for proxy and ours for durable fix.

mike (support): mitigation 1 (client): implement idempotency+dedupe on reconnect. Pass an app-level request_id header and use Last-Event-ID semantics. If you get partial output, check for "data: [PARTIAL]" markers and don't count tokens until final event. Also add a short backoff to avoid immediate retry storms (we saw multiple reconnects).

alex (eng-runtime): mitigation 2 (server/runtime): we'll add a short keepalive comment every 10s (":" line) for these Dedicated pools so proxies see traffic and are less likely to buffer. We'll also add `Cache-Control: no-transform` and flush after each event. But note: some proxies ignore no-transform.

priya (eng-sre): recommended proxy config from our side for F5/Nginx/IIS: 
- ensure `proxy_buffering off` / disable response buffering
- set `proxy_http_version 1.1` and `Connection: ""` to allow chunked transfer
- disable HTML/Error page substitution and any "error page rewrite" features
- increase idle timeout to > 120s for SSE connections

acme-ops: we'll try those. question about billing: why are we charged for duplicate tokens from reconnects?

mia (support): short answer: each request that reaches the model and generates tokens will be billed. Retries that reconverge to the model can create duplicate token consumption. We're opening a billing investigation for r-8c9f2a. For immediate relief we can offer a partial credit if it's clearly caused by our side (e.g., transient 5xx from our ingress).

alex (eng-runtime): looking at our ingress traces for r-8c9f2a we see the upstream returned 200 then later a 502 from proxy. There's a window where the client retried while backend continued streaming — that produced extra tokens. We can implement server-side dedupe for streaming when the same X-Request-ID restarts within short window, but it's non-trivial (closing ticket for runtime work). For now we'll: 
- flag r-8c9f2a for manual refund review
- deploy keepalive comments to dp-33 for 24h test

mike (support): action items: 
- @acme-ops: try client dedupe + backoff + curl repro: 
```
curl -v -H "Accept: text/event-stream" -H "X-Request-ID: r-8c9f2a" \
  -H "Cache-Control: no-transform" --no-buffer https://private-acme.redwood.example/v1/streams
```
- Provide tcpdump pcap and proxy config (iRule / rewrite rules)
- Confirm whether internal proxy inserts an HTML error page or a custom auth page

acme-ops: will do. one more oddity: Windows-based corp proxy seems to split chunks at MSS boundary and that breaks our SSE parser (we're on Node streams). Any recommendations?

alex (eng-runtime): chunk splitting at MSS is normal; SSE clients should be robust to partial frames. Make sure your parser can handle partial lines: don't assume newline-delimited frames arrive full. Also set `maxBuffer` small so you don't accumulate partials into memory. Example Node pattern: 
```js
res.on('data', chunk => {
  buffer += chunk.toString();
  let idx;
  while ((idx = buffer.indexOf('\n\n')) !== -1) {
    const event = buffer.slice(0, idx).trim();
    buffer = buffer.slice(idx + 2);
    // handle event
  }
});
```

priya (eng-sre): final note: if the proxy is doing SSL termination and re-encrypting, make sure it preserves the `Transfer-Encoding: chunked` and doesn't set a `Content-Length`. Also check MTU mismatch on the on-prem ingress path (we saw an environment once where MSS clamping caused mid-chunk TCP RSTs). tcpdump will show lots of retransmits if that's the case.

acme-ops: thanks all. we'll try client-side fixes + share pcap + proxy rules. Appreciate the quick triage — please keep the billing flag open for r-8c9f2a.

mia (support): will keep ticket open and tag eng-runtime/eng-sre. We'll follow up after you attach pcap. Also filing internal follow-up: ENG-RUNTIME-354: keepalive comments rollout to Dedicated pools + billing review for dup tokens.

reconnect-bot: automated note: ticket 354 created, assignees: alex, priya, mia.
